C++ parameter object

Naming rules

suffix Purpose Example

*Ref

refers to an existing object and is only responsible for locating resources.

NodeRef、PortRef、BindingRef

*Params

Complete parameters for an interface call

CreateNodeParams、RuntimeRunParams

*Update

Modify existing configuration, parameters or runtime data

NodeParamUpdate、RuntimeParamsUpdate

It can be understood as follows: * Ref is "Who do I want to operate?" * Params is "I’m going to do a complete thing" * Update is "I want to change something that already exists into something"

Basic writing method

C++ parameter objects are all ordinary struct and can be initialized with aggregates:

client.node().create_node({"my_graph", "ResizeImage"});
client.node().activate_node({"my_graph", node_id});
client.runtime().get_binded_output_value({"my_graph", "result"});

If there are many fields, it is recommended to write the types explicitly so that the code will be clearer:

atom::sdk::NodeConnectionParams connection{
    "my_graph",
    source_node_id, "result",
    target_node_id, "input"
};
client.node().connect_nodes(connection);

Common parameter objects

Graph

Parameter object is used for Field order

CreateGraphParams

graph.create_graph

graph_name, description?

CopyGraphParams

graph.copy_graph

graph_name, new_graph_name

EditGraphNameParams

graph.edit_graph_name

graph_name, new_graph_name

EditGraphCommentParams

graph.edit_graph_comment

graph_name, comment

LoadGraphParams

graph.load_graph

graph_name, file_path

JsonObject

graph.import_extension_nodes_by_path

load_graph extensionNodes in return value

ExportGraphParams

graph.export_graph

graph_name, dl_models_info, custom_nodes

 
auto graph = client.graph().create_graph({"demo_graph", "created by C++ SDK"});
auto graph_status = graph.at("status").get<std::int64_t>();
client.graph().copy_graph({"demo_graph", "demo_graph_backup"});
client.graph().load_graph({"imported_graph", std::filesystem::path("/tmp/demo.atom")});
client.graph().edit_graph_name({"demo_graph", "demo_graph_v2"});
client.graph().edit_graph_comment({"demo_graph_v2", "New process notes"});

Node

Parameter object is used for

NodeRef

Delete, query, activate, initialize, update existing nodes

CreateNodeParams

Create node

CreateDynamicNodeParams

Create dynamic IO node

CopyNodeParams

Copy node

ChangeNodeIOParams

Modify dynamic node input and output

CreateGraphNodeParams

Created from existing subgraphs graph node

GenerateGraphNodeByNodesParams

is packaged and generated by multiple nodes graph node

NodeConnectionParams

Connect or disconnect nodes

PortRef

Read node port data or point cloud

NodeParamUpdate

Set node parameters

NodeBindingUpdate

Set node binding name

EditNodeCommentParams

Modify node remarks

 
auto node = client.node().create_node({"my_graph", "DetectAndSegment", "Detect node"});
std::string node_id = node.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
auto status = node.at("status").get<std::int64_t>();

client.node().activate_node({"my_graph", node_id});
client.node().create_graph_node({"my_graph", "SubFlow", "sub_graph_alpha"});
client.node().generate_graph_node_by_nodes({"my_graph", "PackedNode", {"node-a", "node-b"}});
client.node().edit_node_comment({"my_graph", node_id, "This is a new note"});

The dynamic IO node needs to pass the IO configuration agreed by the server:

client.node().create_dynamic_io_node({
    "my_graph",
    "DynamicNode",
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"inputs":[{"name":"image_in"}]})")
});
client.node().change_node_io({
    "my_graph",
    node_id,
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"outputs":[{"name":"mask_out"}]})")
});

When connecting nodes, the field order is "output first, input last":

client.node().connect_nodes({
    "my_graph",
    resize_node_id, "resized_image",
    detect_node_id, "image"
});

When setting the normal JSON parameter, use atom::sdk::JsonValue for the value:

client.node().set_node_param_data({
    "my_graph",
    node_id,
    "threshold",
    "run_params",
    atom::sdk::JsonValue(0.7)
});

When setting file parameters, use std::filesystem::path as the value, and SDK will be uploaded by file:

client.node().set_node_param_data({
    "my_graph",
    node_id,
    "model",
    "init_params",
    std::filesystem::path("/models/detector.onnx")
});

Binding names are typically "inputs", "outputs", "init_params", or "run_params":

client.node().set_binding_name({
    "my_graph",
    node_id,
    "outputs",
    "results",
    "result"
});

Runtime

Parameter object is used for

RuntimeParamsUpdate

Set shared/run parameters

RuntimeRunParams

submits normal frames or EPICRAW3 and runs the graph

RuntimePassiveBinoFrame Submit EPICRAW3 raw data in

passive_bino mode

RuntimePassiveBinoImage

describes a single original image when constructing EPICRAW3

BindingRef

Read binding output value or raw point cloud

PointCloudRef

Read and parse bound point clouds

RuntimeBindingDataUpdate

Set graph binding input data

RuntimeStrategyParamsUpdate

Set policy parameters

FileParamRef

Query file parameters MD5

SingleNodeParams

runs a single node directly without building a graph. It is recommended to cooperate with run_single_node_no_graph_parsed to automatically parse the output.

RuntimeStrategyParamsUpdate currently only works with PoseListFilter, PickPointFilter, PoseListSorterInXOY、PickPointSorterInXOY、PickPointSorterNew、 PoseListSorter These 6 types of nodes. Its params_data generally starts from runtime().get_node_params_info_with_strategy(…​) Take out paramsData in the return value, modify the fields that need to be updated and then return them as a whole.

atom::sdk::JsonObject run_params;
run_params["threshold"] = 0.7;
client.runtime().set_run_params({"demo_graph", run_params});

auto result = client.runtime().get_binded_output_value({"demo_graph", "result"});

RuntimeRunParams has two input modes:

mode run_mode What should be passed?

Normal mode

"others" or leave blank Put one or more RuntimeFrame in

frames

Passive binocular mode

"passive_bino" Put one RuntimePassiveBinoFrame in

passive_bino_frame

Do not mix the two modes. The normal mode transmits the complete EPICRAW; the passive binocular mode transmits the dedicated passive binocular EPICRAW3. In normal mode, RuntimeFrame is constructed first and then RuntimeRunParams is put in:

auto frame = atom::sdk::RuntimeFrame::from_bytes(
    epicraw_bytes,
    cam_to_base,
    std::nullopt
);

auto run_result = client.runtime().run_graph({"demo_graph", {frame}});
auto status = run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>();

You can also use RuntimeFrame::from_file(…​) to read the file, or RuntimeFrame::from_data(…​) to generate EPICRAW2/3 locally from RuntimePointData, RuntimeImageData and camera parameters. It is recommended to use the RuntimeRunParams factory method in passive binocular mode to avoid forgetting run_mode:

auto run_result = client.runtime().run_graph(
    atom::sdk::RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_file(
        "demo_graph",
        "/data/passive_bino.epicraw",
        cam_to_base));

Use RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_bytes(…​) when there is already EPICRAW3 bytes. Use RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_images(…​) when there are three original images, the image object is RuntimePassiveBinoImage{data, width, height, mat_type}, mat_type uses OpenCV Mat type encoding. params of passive_bino_from_images(…​) needs to contain DepthSrc1, DepthSrc2, TextureSrc and metadata, each of which must contain the following four fields:

json::object camera_params;
camera_params["CameraMatrix"] = json::array{
    2113.997971632298, 0, 1956.222038925553,
    0, 2113.7299751270057, 1505.0473199581195,
    0, 0, 1};
camera_params["CameraDistortion"] = json::array{
    0.049901632334, -0.037810281265, -0.00048319461,
    -0.000276258172, -0.026886293015};
camera_params["CameraRotation"] = json::array{
    0.9995132330503337, -0.005059159488191983, -0.030784766728731865,
    0.004951704878090689, 0.9999813828533568, -0.003565748937897527,
    0.030802233296787017, 0.003411576169582241, 0.999519676430619};
camera_params["CameraTranslation"] = json::array{
    -25.837377992238334, -0.6852264771262435, -4.372034519324568};

json::object passive_bino_params;
passive_bino_params["DepthSrc1"] = camera_params;
passive_bino_params["DepthSrc2"] = camera_params;
passive_bino_params["TextureSrc"] = camera_params;

Easy to make mistakes

1. The connection sequence is output to input

The field order of both NodeConnectionParams and SubGraphConnectionParams is:

graph_name, output_node_id, output_port_name, input_node_id, input_port_name

That is, first write the node and port from which data flows out, and then write the node and port from which data flows in.

2. Use RuntimeService for single-node direct operation.

atom::sdk::SingleNodeParams params;
params.node_name = "MathAddNode";
params.inputs["a"] = atom::sdk::JsonValue(1.0);
params.inputs["b"] = atom::sdk::JsonValue(2.0);

auto result = client.runtime().run_single_node_no_graph_parsed(params);

SingleNodeParams can also be filled in input_data_types / input_point_dims explicitly, but it is usually not required for normal use. When RuntimeService encounters input such as std::filesystem::path or ByteBuffer that needs to be judged, it will press node_name to query the node input port type: * File Input only transmits the path string and does not read the file content. * ColorImage / Image paths will be converted into base64 image lists. * The .ply paths of point cloud ports such as XYZPoints / NormalPoints will be converted to Atom point cloud binary. * When the port type cannot be queried, ByteBuffer or path content is still uploaded as a file field according to the old rules. If using the recommended run_single_node_no_graph_parsed, SingleNodeParams can also be filled in explicitly output_data_types / output_point_dims: * output_data_types tells SDK which outputs are of XYZPoints, ColorImage, etc. parsable types. * output_point_dims is used for point cloud output dimension prompts; XYZPoints defaults to 3, NormalPoints/RGBPoints defaults to 6. * When not filled in, SDK will press node_name to query the node output port type; if the server returns raw bytes, it needs to be able to determine the only point cloud output port.

3. RuntimeFrame field name is different from the server field name

The field name in C++ is cam_to_base. SDK will be converted into cam2Base required by the server when packaging the request. cam_to_base The server currently only supports the rotation vector form: [x, y, z, rx, ry, rz] with length 6 (translation + Rodrigues rotation vector), and does not support 4x4/3x4 matrices; SDK will verify the length when constructing RuntimeFrame/RuntimePassiveBinoFrame, and will throw std::invalid_argument if it is not satisfied.

4. The simple interface still transfers strings directly

The following interfaces still retain direct string parameters:

client.graph().open_graph("my_graph");
client.graph().run_graph("my_graph");
client.runtime().load_graph("my_graph");
client.runtime().get_meta_info("my_graph");

If an interface requires multiple business fields, use parameter objects.
